case_title: Ex-Gunner Virender Prasad v. Union of India & Anr.
statutory_provisions: Army Act s.69; Code of Criminal Procedure s.433-A
mitigating_circumstances: Surrendered immediately, excellent conduct in jail, served more than 14 years of sentence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder and sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, a gunner, was posted at a radar post in Kashmir. The deceased, a fellow gunner, was on good terms with the accused. On the date of the incident, the accused shot the deceased while in a state of sleep. The accused claimed he fired the rifle under a delusion that there was a terrorist attack. He immediately came out of his tent, surrendered to his superiors, and confessed his guilt. An investigation was conducted, and the case was registered before the Chief Judicial Magistrate. The accused was charged under Section 69 of the Army Act for committing a civil offence of murder. A Court Martial was held, and the accused was found guilty and sentenced to life imprisonment. The accused challenged the conviction before the Armed Forces Tribunal, which dismissed the appeal. The accused had served more than 14 years of his sentence and had excellent conduct in jail.
